title: Truncation tower reconstructs a complex under bounded local cohomological dimension

from.place: proof, first step, truncation tower (via Stacks 08D3)

statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Assume there exist an integer $d\geq0$ and a basis $\mathcal B$ for the topology of $X$ such that $H^p(U,H^q(E))=0$ for all $U\in\mathcal B$, all $p>d$ and all $q<0$, where $H^q(E)$ is the $q$-th cohomology sheaf and $H^p(U,-)$ is sheaf cohomology of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on $U$ [pqf-def-cohomology]. For $n\geq0$ let $E_n=\tau_{\geq-n}E$ be the standard truncations [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], with their canonical transition maps $E_{n+1}\to E_n$ and the canonical maps $E\to E_n$. Then $E$, together with a morphism $E\to\prod_nE_n$ whose components are the canonical maps, is a derived limit $R\varprojlim_nE_n$ in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-derived-limit]; that is, the canonical map $E\to R\varprojlim_nE_n$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_X)$.
